result.title: VideoSlate: Stateful Commit Control for Temporally Grounded Agentic Video Reasoning
result.summary: Agentic video reasoning systems gather and assess video evidence across stages, selecting relevant spans as visual evidence for answering questions. New candidates and observations prompt reassessment of the current span, but revisions can correct localization errors or discard useful evidence already present in the adopted span. Systems therefore need to connect evidence organization across stages with temporal state control, allowing accumulated information to jointly inform revision assessment while explicit adoption decisions govern how assessment outcomes affect downstream visual evidence. We introduce VideoSlate, a stateful commit-control framework built around shared evidence. A typed evidence blackboard links candidate spans, provenance, construction, and verifier observations, enabling an incumbent-relative certifier to assess revision support from the candidate, current span, and related proposals. Based on certification, the controller authorizes a revision or retains the current span, separating evidence accumulation from state updates and recording each decision and its evidence on the blackboard. Extensive evaluations across video grounding and grounded question-answering benchmarks show that VideoSlate can improve temporal localization through selective revision.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VideoSlate，一个以共享证据为中心的有状态提交控制框架：用类型化证据「黑板」连接候选片段、来源、构造与验证观察，由相对当前采纳片段的 certifier 判断修订支持度，控制器据此决定修订或保留，从而把证据积累与状态更新分离，用于视频时序定位与 grounded 问答。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「采纳/保留」提交控制与证据积累—状态更新分离，直接对应 LVR 关注的证据筛选与 STOP/停止决策问题，可供核查显式采纳决策如何约束下游视觉证据的流向与修订时机。
